summary: Stage A web audit for brief 3 (lower 48), read-only, revised after an independent review. The web app is California-shaped in six places: overview frame/wording, time zone, fire record (CAL FIRE down to the fetch path), search (California Gazetteer; a lon/lat order guess that fails east of 90 W), official panels (Cal OES, NWS 'in California', California-only overview outlines) and imagery labels (GOES-West). BLOCKERs: (1) every time is Pacific via lib/time.ts TZ (214 call sites, 43 files; laWallToMs hard-codes PDT/PST), and the user's mixed clock changes Public strings even in CA; (2) no clustering: with real data (1,334 fires, 179 active injected; 244 active nationally) today's overview draws an amber blob and 42 labels, 11 of them on fires under 10 ac, while only 12 of 74 fires >= 20,000 ac are labelled; (3) the record is CAL FIRE end to end and official/calfire.ts:89 would show a WFIGS row as 'CAL FIRE incident record' once calfire_uid aliases uid; (4) official panels outside CA; (5) a pasted lon-first pair east of 90 W (e.g. '-84.39, 33.75') lands at 84.39 S with an 'ok' message. Proposed: one tz+clock formatter (useTimeFormat; zone from backend R2/R3, no county table); three MapLibre sources (pinned active >= 5,000 ac + open fire, clustered active, clustered other; size-aware bubbles by max_acres; labels by acres) - a browser prototype gives 48 marks instead of 1,334 at the national view, no new dependency; source-neutral record fetch (record_source -> /api/official/incident-record); national NWS wording written out; lat/lon plausibility; coverage via /api/geo/lookup; accuracy label P0; hand-written windowed list with keyboard/ARIA design; gzip with the national list. Scale (WFIGS count-only): 2026 >= 300 ac lower 48 = 1,178 (35 states); 2025 = 861 (38 states); 2025 >= 100 ac = 1,664; active now 244 (112 <= 1 ac, 43 no size). Round-2 decisions answer all earlier user questions; none remain open.

known_issues: Stage A audit only; nothing fixed.

The national injection uses WFIGS Current for non-CA actives and CAL FIRE fixture lists for CA (3 active), so it shows 179 of the 244 lower-48 active fires; the CA WFIGS gap-fill (round 2 item 2) is not simulated.
The clustering prototype is a throwaway in the page (scratchpad script), not a tested implementation; parameters (radii, 5,000-ac pin threshold, zoom steps) are starting values for the builder.
Overview list render timing (424 ms, first pass) is a single sample in a software-rendered sandbox; frame rates are not meaningful without a GPU.
Pre-existing phone bugs seen in evidence: the map controls row covers the search message; opening the overview list sheet refits the map so fires sit behind the sheet.
Backend-baked Pacific strings (build/observed.py:200 etc.) are outside web scope (backend R7, validation G6).
notes_for_integrator: CONTRACT §14 (planner): IncidentSummary.state, time_zone, record_source ('calfire'|'wfigs'), record_agency, record_url, uid (calfire_uid deprecated alias), accuracy_region; manifest.time_zone/state; states[] on official/extras answers; time_zone per NWS alert; GET /api/geo/lookup -> {state, state_name, time_zone, supported}; GET /api/official/incident-record (kind incident_record); detections_24h (keep _ca one release); gzip on /api/incidents (backend R17, ship with the national list). SPEC §4.2: 'The UI shows each fire's local time with its zone abbreviation.' Keep existing CA ids resolving.

Safety: official/calfire.ts:89 must check record_source === 'calfire' before using the summary fallback, or a WFIGS record is labelled 'CAL FIRE incident record' as soon as calfire_uid aliases uid. Land W4 in the same wave as backend R2/R10.

Time: tz and clock are required arguments in lib/time.ts (typecheck enumerates the 214 call sites); useTimeFormat() = {tz: manifest.time_zone ?? summary.time_zone, clock: Public preset ? '12h' : '24h'}; replace laWallToMs's 420/480 candidates with a generic offset search; zone only from backend R2/R3 (no county table, no NWS /points). Public CA strings and about 47 test lines change by the user's round-2 decision; Command/Forensic CA strings stay identical.

Overview: three sources (fx-overview-pinned unclustered: active >= 5,000 ac + the open card's fire, read by selection ring/chip/labels; fx-overview-active clustered r28/max z6; fx-overview-other r40/max z7); active bubbles sized by max_acres; small actives (< 10 ac or no size) as plain dots; label priority by acres; cluster click capped at z8 (< FOCUS_IN_ZOOM 8.5); hidden fires removed before setData.

List windowing is hand-written (no react-window); FireList keyboard (OverviewPanel.tsx:74-77) must scroll the target into the window before focusing, with aria-setsize/aria-posinset. Keep the 2025 >= 100 ac switch nationally (1,664 rows).

Search: geodesy.ts lat/lon order must try both orders against a lower-48 heuristic box (tests: Atlanta, Miami, Boston, Houston, LA); likelyMissingWestSign generalised to the lower 48. Coverage messages come from /api/geo/lookup, never client boxes.

Cross-audit: evacuations.md E-R1/R3/R5/R7/R8 for the not-available state, wording, time basis and NWS-relayed local messages; validation.md §5 for the accuracy label wording (W10, P0) and G15 skill-table colour; backend.md R2/R3/R10/R11/R15/R16/R17/R18.

User questions: none open. Round 2 answered Q1 (mixed clock) and backend Q2 (all active fires); Q2-Q5 are round-2 defaults (active-only groups, list in view, whole lower 48 on phones, cameras CA only).
